title: Curve projective dense completion
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a separated finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with $\dim X\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There exist a projective $k$-scheme $C$ [def-kun-projective] of dimension at most one and an open immersion $a:X\to C$ [def-weil-open-immersion] whose image is dense and scheme-theoretically dense (the map $\mathcal O_C\to a_*\mathcal O_X$ is injective), with complement a finite set of closed points. If $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], $C$ can be taken reduced. If $X$ is empty, $C$ can be empty.

source.place: Tag 0BXV, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion; proof: scheme-theoretic closure, whose reduction agrees over reduced X

proof.text: First $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian since its only affine ring $k$ has just the ideals $0$ and $k$, and its space is a singleton. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], every open of $X$ is quasi-compact: for an open cover of an open $V$, choose a maximal finite union of covering opens using the minimal-complement assertion; if that union misses a point of $V$, adjoining a covering open through that point contradicts maximality. Consequently the inverse image of any affine open under any morphism from $X$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tags 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology) and 01P0 (lemma-morphism-Noetherian-schemes-quasi-compact); finite type input: Morphisms Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-dim-one-quasi-projective] to the separated finite type $k$-scheme $X$ with $\dim X\le1$. Obtain a closed immersion $X\to U$ followed by an open immersion $U\to\mathbf P^N_k$ over $k$, hence an immersion $h:X\to\mathbf P^N_k$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Step 1 makes $h$ quasi-compact. Take its constructed scheme-theoretic image $C$ with closed immersion $i:C\to\mathbf P^N_k$ and factor map $a:X\to C$, supplied by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], $a$ is an open immersion with topologically and scheme-theoretically dense image. The latter means exactly that $\mathcal O_C\to a_*\mathcal O_X$ is injective. Give $C$ the structure map induced by $i$; the factorization is over $k$, and the closed immersion into $\mathbf P^N_k$ makes $C$ projective by [def-kun-projective].

source.place: Tag 0BXV (lemma-dim-1-projective-completion), first three sentences; inputs: Tag 0A25 (lemma-dim-1-quasi-projective), Morphisms Tags 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image) and 01RG (lemma-quasi-compact-immersion)

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper], the projective structure map $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper, and thus of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the same Noetherian $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to conclude that $C$ is Noetherian. This verifies the finite type and Noetherian hypotheses needed in the following dimension and boundary steps.

source.place: Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), applied to a projective morphism; Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian)

proof.text: Use [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] with the closed subset $C$ itself to write $C=\bigcup_{j=1}^r Z_j$ as its finitely many irreducible components; by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] each has a generic point $\eta_j$. Each $\eta_j$ belongs to $a(X)$. Indeed, if $\eta_j$ lay in another component $Z_l$, its closure $Z_j$ would be contained in $Z_l$, contradicting maximality of the distinct components. Thus $C\setminus\bigcup_{l\ne j}Z_l$ is an open containing $\eta_j$, so density of $a(X)$ gives a point of $a(X)\cap Z_j$. As $a(X)\cap Z_j$ is nonempty open in $Z_j$, it contains its generic point: otherwise its closed complement in $Z_j$ would contain $\eta_j$ and hence all of $Z_j$.

source.place: Tag 0BXV (lemma-dim-1-projective-completion), generic-point argument; Properties Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components) and Schemes Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober)

proof.text: Identify $X$ with $a(X)$ and let $D_j=Z_j\cap X$. This is a nonempty irreducible closed subset of $X$, with generic point $\eta_j$, since the closure of $\eta_j$ in the subspace $X$ is $Z_j\cap X$. Apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] first to $Z_j\subseteq C$ and then to $D_j\subseteq X$, both in finite type $k$-schemes. By [def-weil-open-immersion], the structure sheaf on $X$ is the restriction of that on $C$. Taking germs at $\eta_j$ gives an isomorphism of local $k$-algebras; quotienting by their corresponding maximal ideals identifies the residue fields, giving $\dim Z_j=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_C(\eta_j)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_X(\eta_j)=\dim D_j\le\dim X\le1$. The inequality is immediate from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]: a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $D_j$ is also such a chain in $X$, since $D_j$ is closed in $X$. Finally any irreducible closed subset of $C$ is contained in some $Z_j$: it is covered by its intersections with the finite family of closed $Z_j$, so irreducibility forces one intersection to be the whole subset. Thus every chain counted in $\dim C$ lies in a $Z_j$ and has length at most one. Hence $\dim C\le1$, including mixed zero- and one-dimensional components.

source.place: Tag 0BXV (lemma-dim-1-projective-completion), dimension sentence; Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), part (6), item Tag 0B1C (item-dimension-irreducible-trdeg)

proof.text: Put $E=C\setminus a(X)$, a closed subset. Every $b\in E$ is closed in $C$: choose a component $Z_j$ containing $b$; its generic point $\eta_j$ is in $a(X)$ by step 4 and differs from $b$. If $b$ had a distinct specialization $c$, there would be a strict chain $\overline{\{c\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{b\}}\subsetneq Z_j$ of irreducible closed subsets of $C$, contradicting $\dim C\le1$. Strictness follows from uniqueness of generic points in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], $E$ is a finite union of irreducible closed subsets $T_l$. Each $T_l$ is closed in $C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] supplies its generic point $t_l$. Since $t_l\in E$ is closed in $C$, $T_l=\overline{\{t_l\}}=\{t_l\}$. Thus $E$ is a finite set of closed points, with the empty boundary allowed.

source.place: Tag 0BXV (lemma-dim-1-projective-completion), last sentence, expanded using Properties Tag 0BA8 and Schemes Tag 01IS

proof.text: If $X$ is reduced, the same $C$ is reduced; no normalization is necessary. For any open $V\subseteq C$, a nilpotent section $s\in\mathcal O_C(V)$ restricts to a nilpotent section of $\mathcal O_X(a^{-1}V)$, which is zero by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The scheme-theoretic density supplied by [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] makes this restriction injective, so $s=0$. Thus all rings of sections of $C$ are reduced, which is precisely the equivalent criterion in [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Tags 01J0 (definition-reduced) and 01J1 (lemma-reduced); elementary consequence of the scheme-theoretic density from Morphisms Tag 01RG

proof.text: If $X$ is empty, the constructed $C$ is empty as well: step 2 makes the empty image dense, and the closure of the empty set is empty. The dimension bound, empty finite boundary, and reducedness assertions are then vacuous; the same closed immersion $C\to\mathbf P^N_k$ still supplies projectivity. This establishes the allowed empty case without a nonemptiness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0BXV (lemma-dim-1-projective-completion), construction applied to the empty scheme

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BXV (lemma-dim-1-projective-completion), proof; generic-point and boundary arguments expanded, with the elementary reduced and empty cases

lean.statement: theorem exists_projective_dense_completion_of_dim_le_one {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) : ∃ (C : Scheme.{u}) (g : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (a : X ⟶ C), IsHProjective g ∧ topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 1 ∧ IsOpenImmersion a ∧ a ≫ g = X ↘ Spec (.of k) ∧ DenseRange a ∧ (∀ U : C.Opens, Function.Injective (a.app U)) ∧ (Set.range a)ᶜ.Finite ∧ (∀ c : C, c ∉ Set.range a → IsClosed ({c} : Set C)) ∧ (IsReduced X → IsReduced C) ∧ (IsEmpty X → IsEmpty C)
